## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Define the tutorial packaging format

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format: the structure that makes a
tutorial a versioned, independently testable artifact. The format specifies
tutorial metadata, pinned image references, and a validation manifest, so that
tutorials can be versioned and validated independently of Dashboard releases.
It is the shared interface that the tutorial gallery's launch mechanics and
all authored tutorials build against.

## Scope

- Specify the tutorial metadata schema (identity, journey classification,
  versioning) that a packaged tutorial carries.
- Specify how pinned images are referenced so a tutorial runs against known
  image versions rather than floating tags.
- Specify the validation manifest: what a packaged tutorial must declare so
  it can be tested (and re-tested) against a platform release without a
  Dashboard change.
- Provide a reference example of a tutorial packaged per the format that
  passes the format's validation end-to-end.
- Publish the specification where both content authors and the Dashboard
  gallery implementers can build against it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines the tutorial metadata schema,
  the pinned image reference mechanism, and the contents of the validation
  manifest.
- A reference tutorial packaged per the format passes the format's own
  validation.
- Versioning independence is demonstrated: a conforming tutorial can be
  versioned and validated as a packaged artifact, with no Dashboard release
  required to add, update, or validate it.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases. (Epic priority is P0 by inheritance:
  this format gates all P0 work in the strategy.)

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, browsable
gallery of tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with one
click. Launching a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project
with the tutorial notebook loaded; launching a pipeline tutorial imports the
pipeline into the user's project.

## Scope

- Add the tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard (listing curated
  tutorials with their metadata).
- Implement one-click launch of a tutorial into the user's own project:
  - notebook tutorials open a workbench with the tutorial notebook,
  - pipeline tutorials import the pipeline into the project.
- Consume the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) so any tutorial packaged per the format is launchable — the
  gallery must not hard-code individual tutorials.
- Keep the gallery within existing Dashboard conventions (projects, CR-based
  interaction, feature administration), leaving specific configuration
  mechanics to the implementing team.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user with a project, when they open the tutorial gallery, then
  curated tutorials are listed with their packaged metadata.
- Given a notebook tutorial listed in the gallery, when the user launches it,
  then a workbench is opened in their project with the tutorial notebook
  loaded.
- Given a pipeline tutorial listed in the gallery, when the user launches it,
  then the pipeline is imported into their project.
- Launching a tutorial into the user's project requires a single user action.
- A tutorial packaged per the tutorial packaging format is launchable by the
  gallery without gallery-side changes specific to that tutorial (validated
  with a tutorial packaged per the format).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline).

# Author five curated notebook tutorials

## Description

This epic authors the notebook portion of the curated tutorial set: five
maintained, tested tutorials covering the core notebook-based journeys —
first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first
RAG app. Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and
tested against the current release, so it can be launched from the tutorial
gallery.

## Scope

- Author the five curated notebook tutorials:
  1. First workbench — creating and using a first workbench.
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — deploying a first model.
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest).
- Validate each tutorial against the current platform release via its
  validation manifest.
- Keep content scope to the tutorial notebooks themselves; the gallery that
  launches them and the pipeline tutorial are handled elsewhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five curated notebook tutorials exist, one per journey: first workbench,
  data prep, first training run, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest).
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest against the current platform
  release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, notebook portion): Six curated tutorials exist covering the core
  journeys — this epic delivers the five notebook journeys (first workbench,
  data prep, first training run, first deployment, first RAG app), each
  tested against the current release.

# Document the tutorial gallery and contribution process

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for the tutorial gallery: user-facing
documentation on using the gallery (discovering and launching tutorials into
a project) and contributor-facing documentation on the process for authoring
and contributing new tutorials. Documentation follows the Red Hat docs
content process.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside the documentation set):

- Using the tutorial gallery:
  - discovering and browsing available tutorials,
  - launching a notebook tutorial (workbench opened with the notebook),
  - launching a pipeline tutorial (pipeline imported into the project).
- Contributing new tutorials:
  - packaging a tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
    images, validation manifest),
  - validating a tutorial against a platform release,
  - the review and publication path for new tutorials (process only — no
    submission tooling this release, per the strategy's out-of-scope list).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery: discovering
  tutorials and launching both notebook and pipeline tutorials into a
  project.
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials:
  packaging per the format, validation, and the review path.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and tutorials (accuracy of steps verified against the shipped behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials. (Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring
  priority exception: strategy priority Major → P1.)

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

## Triage Outcome

Neither Step 0 check fired. The strategy is not below-threshold: the problem
statement itself identifies three architecturally distinct work streams —
product code (Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), authored content (six
curated tutorials across notebook and pipeline surfaces owned by different
teams), and documentation — which warrant separate PR review cycles. It is not
docs-only: the Dashboard requires code changes. Full decomposition follows.

## Strategy Structure Notes

- Affected Components: Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines,
  Documentation (listed without change descriptions or owner teams).
- HLRs: HLR-1 (P0, gallery + one-click launch), HLR-2 (P0, six curated tested
  tutorials), HLR-3 (P1, tutorial packaging format), HLR-4 (P2, documentation).
- Open Questions: none. No risks, assumptions, conditional ADRs, or pending
  reviews are stated — no Investigation epics are warranted.
- Owner teams are not given in the strategy; they were taken from
  `.context/architecture-context/` (see Component Mapping Notes).
- No Staff Engineer Input section is present.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Define the tutorial packaging format | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 | Author five curated notebook tutorials | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 | Author the first-pipeline tutorial | Implementation | RHOAI Pipelines | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 | Document the tutorial gallery and contribution process | Implementation | RHOAI Docs | P1 |

Notes on the list:

- E001 carries HLR-3 (P1) but is raised to P0 by priority inheritance: every
  P0 epic in the strategy (E002, E003, E004) builds against the packaging
  format, so E001 blocks all P0 work.
- E005 is `implementation_type: docs-authoring`. Per the docs-authoring
  priority exception its priority derives from the strategy frontmatter
  (`priority: Major` → P1), not from HLR-4's P2 label, and it does not push
  priority upstream.
- E002, E003, E004 run in parallel once E001 lands: different components,
  different teams, different repos, no shared artifacts beyond the format.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 Tutorial packaging format] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 Dashboard gallery]
    E001 --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 Notebook tutorials]
    E001 --> E004[RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 Pipeline tutorial]
    E001 --> E005[RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 Documentation]
    E002 --> E005
    E003 --> E005
    E004 --> E005
```

Critical path: E001 → E002 → E005 (length 3).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The gallery's launch mechanics consume the packaging format's metadata and validation manifest as an interface the Dashboard code builds against — not a mere configuration reference. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | Notebook tutorials are packaged and validated per the format; content cannot be finalized before the format is defined. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The pipeline tutorial is packaged and validated per the same format. |
| E001 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | docs-authoring epic blocked by every Implementation epic. |
| E002 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Docs describe the built gallery. |
| E003 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Docs describe the built tutorials. |
| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Docs describe the built tutorials. |
| E002 ∥ E003 ∥ E004 | Rules 14/15 (parallel) | Different components, teams, and repos with no shared artifacts once the format exists; the gallery does not produce anything the tutorial content builds against. |

No konflux-onboarding, license-validation, or repo-onboarding epics were
generated: all three code components (Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science
Pipelines) are Konflux-onboarded GA components per their architecture-context
files, so Rule 25 build-pipeline ACs do not apply.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Gallery UI plus both launch paths (workbench with notebook, pipeline import). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E003, RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 | Split by component/team boundary: five notebook tutorials (Workbenches) and the pipeline tutorial (RHOAI Pipelines). Together they cover all six journeys. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Epic priority raised to P0 by inheritance — it gates all P0 work. Not a bundling decision: the HLR has its own epic. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 | docs-authoring priority exception: strategy priority Major → P1. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements. No redundant/overlapping
HLR pairs exist (gallery mechanics, tutorial content, packaging format, and
docs are distinct capabilities on distinct surfaces).

## Component Mapping Notes

- E001's work spans the strategy's Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines, and
  Dashboard components (the format is consumed by all three), but is assigned
  the single most-relevant canonical component **Notebooks**: the tutorials are
  predominantly notebooks and the pinned-image aspect maps to the workbench
  imagestreams that the Notebooks architecture context describes as maintained
  by the platform.
- E002 → component **Dashboard** (team RHOAI Dashboard), E003 → **Notebooks**
  (team Workbenches), E004 → **Data Science Pipelines** (team RHOAI Pipelines),
  E005 → **Documentation** (team assumed RHOAI Docs) — all verbatim canonical
  names from `.context/rhai-components.txt`.
- The **Documentation** component has no architecture-context file. No
  onboarding chain was generated: Documentation is a docs-process component
  delivered through the Red Hat docs content process (`docs-authoring`
  implementation type), not a new code component needing a repo or build
  pipeline.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking):** the strategy has no Impacted
   Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Acceptance Criteria section (no
   Given/When/Then with "measured by" clauses), and no Non-Functional
   Requirements. Owner teams were inferred from architecture context and epic
   acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs.
2. **E003 size over the ~2-week guideline:** authoring and validating five
   tested notebook tutorials is estimated at roughly 2–3 sprints of content
   effort (the strategy provides no effort arithmetic). Kept whole because all
   five tutorials share one packaging format, one validation approach, and one
   content review pipeline — splitting them would duplicate format-conformance
   and validation setup and fragment a single content stream. Re-split trigger:
   if the tutorial set exceeds 3 sprints of effort, or any single tutorial
   grows its own engineering track (e.g., the RAG tutorial needs new sample
   infrastructure beyond a notebook), split E003 by journey group (workbench/
   data-prep vs training/deployment/RAG).
3. **Ongoing-maintenance scope trap (non-blocking):** HLR-2 requires tutorials
   "tested against the current release" — a one-time gate at delivery. The
   strategy is silent on re-validating tutorials against future releases;
   that operational treadmill is out of scope here and should be planned
   separately if wanted.
4. **Docs priority inversion flag (expected):** HLR-4 is P2 but E005 is P1 by
   the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy `priority: Major`). This is
   per-spec, not an inconsistency.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — the strategy has no external dependencies with uncertain
timing; all work is internal to the platform's teams.
